problem: The grid cell says "Many owners, one VO". This contradicts the lead, where a VO is tied to one project. A single grid usually serves several VOs at the same time, so "one VO" reads as if a grid can have only one.
fix: Write "Many owners; access through one or more VOs" so the cell matches the definition of a VO as a per-project sharing group.

where: Section 1, first paragraph and Quiz Q1
problem: The VO is defined only as the set of users allowed to share. Standard definitions include the resource providers and the sharing rules, not just users. A student may answer Q1 with users alone and lose marks.
fix: Define it as the set of users, sites and resources that agree to share under one set of rules for a project; the quiz answer should say "users, sites and resources sharing under agreed rules".

problem: "Brokers, allocation and directories" puts plain allocation in the collective layer. Allocating one site's own resource is a resource-layer job; the collective layer does co-allocation and brokering across several sites. As written, the two layers overlap and the student cannot tell them apart.
fix: Write "brokers, co-allocation across sites and directories", and keep single-resource allocation with the resource layer.

problem: The schedule silently assumes that all three sites are free from the same instant and that the job can run on all 160 CPUs at once. Real grids queue jobs at each site, so the 6.67-hour answer is only valid under these assumptions, which are never stated.
fix: Add one line: assume all three sites are idle at t = 0 and the job scales to 160 parallel processes; otherwise add queue waiting time per site.
